{{Short description|Result in probability theory}}
In [[probability theory]], '''Lévy’s continuity theorem''', or '''Lévy's convergence theorem''',<ref name=W>{{cite book
  | last = Williams | first = D. | authorlink = David Williams (mathematician)
  | title = Probability with Martingales
  | year = 1991
  | publisher = Cambridge University Press
  | isbn = 0-521-40605-6 |at=section 18.1
  }}</ref> named after the French [[mathematician]] [[Paul Lévy (mathematician)|Paul Lévy]], connects [[convergence in distribution]] of the sequence of random variables with [[pointwise convergence]] of their [[Characteristic function (probability theory)|characteristic functions]]. 
This theorem is the basis for one approach to prove the [[central limit theorem]] and is one of the major theorems concerning characteristic functions.

==Statement==

Suppose we have
{{unordered list
|1= a sequence of [[random variable]]s <math display="inline"> \{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty</math>, not necessarily sharing a common [[probability space]],
|2= the sequence of corresponding [[Characteristic function (probability theory)|characteristic function]]s <math display="inline"> \{\varphi_n\}_{n=1}^\infty</math>, which by definition are 
: <math>\varphi_n(t) = \operatorname{E} \left[ e^{itX_n} \right] \quad \forall t\in\mathbb{R},\ \forall n\in\mathbb{N},</math>
where <math>\operatorname{E}</math> is the [[expected value]] operator.
}}

If the sequence of characteristic functions [[pointwise convergence|converges pointwise]] to some function <math>\varphi</math>
:<math>\varphi_n(t)\to\varphi(t) \quad \forall t\in\mathbb{R},</math>
then the following statements become equivalent:
{{unordered list
|1= <math>X_n</math> [[Convergence of random variables#Convergence in distribution|converges in distribution]] to some [[random variable]] ''X''
:<math>X_n\ \xrightarrow{\mathcal D}\ X,</math>
i.e. the cumulative distribution functions corresponding to random variables converge at every continuity point of the c.d.f. of&nbsp;''X'';
|2= <math display="inline"> \{X_n\}_{n=1}^\infty</math> is [[Tightness of measures|tight]]: 
:<math>\lim_{x\to\infty}\left( \sup_n \operatorname{P}\big[\, |X_n|>x \,\big]\right) = 0;</math>
|3= <math>\varphi(t)</math> is a characteristic function of some random variable ''X'';
|4= <math>\varphi(t)</math> is a [[continuous function]] of ''t'';
|5= <math>\varphi(t)</math> is [[continuous function|continuous]] at ''t''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.
}}

== Proof ==
Rigorous proofs of this theorem are available.<ref name=W/><ref>{{cite book |last=Fristedt |first=B. E. |last2=Gray |first2=L. F. |year=1996 |title=A modern approach to probability theory |publisher=Birkhäuser |location=Boston |isbn=0-8176-3807-5 |at=Theorems 14.15 and 18.21 }}</ref>
